answer: In a Sybil-resistant mechanism, AI agents utilize a proof-of-stake system where each agent is assigned a unique digital pearl, representing its stake. When an agent broadcasts a signal to the network, it must include a cryptographic proof that its stake was randomly selected. This proof is verified by other agents, who check that the signal is consistent with the relic - a publicly available, tamper-evident ledger of all stakes. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities must control a large number of pearls, making it costly to manipulate the network.
